import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

namespace EnergyBootstrap

noncomputable section

def rowDegree {I J : Type*} [Fintype J] (R : I → J → Prop) (i : I) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact (Finset.univ.filter (R i)).card

def colDegree {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] (R : I → J → Prop) (j : J) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => R i j)).card

def edgeSum {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype J]
    (R : I → J → Prop) (a : I → ℝ) (b : J → ℝ) : ℝ := by
  classical
  exact ∑ i, ∑ j, if R i j then a i * b j else 0

theorem graphSchur {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype J]
    (R : I → J → Prop) (a : I → ℝ) (b : J → ℝ) (r s : ℕ)
    (hr : ∀ i, rowDegree R i ≤ r) (hs : ∀ j, colDegree R j ≤ s) :
    (edgeSum R a b) ^ 2 ≤
      ((r : ℝ) * (s : ℝ)) * (∑ i, a i ^ 2) * (∑ j, b j ^ 2) := by
  classical
  let E : Finset (I × J) := Finset.univ.filter (fun e => R e.1 e.2)
  have hE : edgeSum R a b = ∑ e ∈ E, a e.1 * b e.2 := by
    simp [edgeSum, E, Finset.sum_filter, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
  have hAeq : (∑ e ∈ E, a e.1 ^ 2) =
      ∑ i, (rowDegree R i : ℝ) * a i ^ 2 := by
    simp only [E, Finset.sum_filter, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i hi
    rw [← Finset.sum_filter]
    simp [rowDegree, nsmul_eq_mul]
  have hBeq : (∑ e ∈ E, b e.2 ^ 2) =
      ∑ j, (colDegree R j : ℝ) * b j ^ 2 := by
    simp only [E, Finset.sum_filter, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro j hj
    rw [← Finset.sum_filter]
    simp [colDegree, nsmul_eq_mul]
  have hA : (∑ e ∈ E, a e.1 ^ 2) ≤ (r : ℝ) * ∑ i, a i ^ 2 := by
    rw [hAeq, Finset.mul_sum]
    apply Finset.sum_le_sum
    intro i hi
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (by exact_mod_cast hr i) (sq_nonneg _)
  have hB : (∑ e ∈ E, b e.2 ^ 2) ≤ (s : ℝ) * ∑ j, b j ^ 2 := by
    rw [hBeq, Finset.mul_sum]
    apply Finset.sum_le_sum
    intro j hj
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (by exact_mod_cast hs j) (sq_nonneg _)
  calc
    (edgeSum R a b) ^ 2 = (∑ e ∈ E, a e.1 * b e.2) ^ 2 := by rw [hE]
    _ ≤ (∑ e ∈ E, a e.1 ^ 2) * ∑ e ∈ E, b e.2 ^ 2 :=
      Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq E (fun e => a e.1) (fun e => b e.2)
    _ ≤ ((r : ℝ) * ∑ i, a i ^ 2) * ((s : ℝ) * ∑ j, b j ^ 2) :=
      mul_le_mul hA hB (by positivity) (by positivity)
    _ = _ := by ring

abbrev BoundedTuple (n M : ℕ) := Fin n → Fin (M + 1)

def indexSum {n M : ℕ} (x : BoundedTuple n M) : ℤ :=
  ∑ i, ((x i).val : ℤ)

theorem tupleSumCount (n M : ℕ) (target : ℤ) :
    Fintype.card {x : BoundedTuple (n + 1) M // indexSum x = target} ≤
      (M + 1) ^ n := by
  classical
  let drop : {x : BoundedTuple (n + 1) M // indexSum x = target} →
      BoundedTuple n M := fun x i => x.1 i.succ
  have hinj : Function.Injective drop := by
    intro x y h
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext i
    refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun k => congrFun h k) i
    apply Fin.ext
    have hx := x.2
    have hy := y.2
    simp only [indexSum, Fin.sum_univ_succ] at hx hy
    have ht : (∑ k : Fin n, ((x.1 k.succ).val : ℤ)) =
        ∑ k : Fin n, ((y.1 k.succ).val : ℤ) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro k hk
      exact congrArg (fun z : Fin (M + 1) => (z.val : ℤ)) (congrFun h k)
    have hz : ((x.1 0).val : ℤ) = ((y.1 0).val : ℤ) := by omega
    exact_mod_cast hz
  calc
    _ ≤ Fintype.card (BoundedTuple n M) := Fintype.card_le_of_injective drop hinj
    _ = (M + 1) ^ n := by simp [BoundedTuple]

theorem modeSumSchur (p q M : ℕ) (target : ℤ)
    (a : BoundedTuple (p + 1) M → ℝ)
    (b : BoundedTuple (q + 1) M → ℝ) :
    (edgeSum (fun l r => indexSum r - indexSum l = target) a b) ^ 2 ≤
      ((M : ℝ) + 1) ^ (p + q) * (∑ l, a l ^ 2) * (∑ r, b r ^ 2) := by
  classical
  have hr : ∀ l : BoundedTuple (p + 1) M,
      rowDegree (fun l r => indexSum r - indexSum l = target) l ≤
        (M + 1) ^ q := by
    intro l
    simpa [rowDegree, Fintype.card_subtype, sub_eq_iff_eq_add] using
      tupleSumCount q M (target + indexSum l)
  have hs : ∀ r : BoundedTuple (q + 1) M,
      colDegree (fun l r => indexSum r - indexSum l = target) r ≤
        (M + 1) ^ p := by
    intro r
    have hp : ∀ l : BoundedTuple (p + 1) M,
        (indexSum r - indexSum l = target) ↔
          (indexSum l = indexSum r - target) := by
      intro l
      omega
    simpa [colDegree, Fintype.card_subtype, hp] using
      tupleSumCount p M (indexSum r - target)
  have h := graphSchur (fun l r => indexSum r - indexSum l = target)
    a b ((M + 1) ^ q) ((M + 1) ^ p) hr hs
  push_cast at h
  rw [← pow_add, Nat.add_comm q p] at h
  exact h

def pathSquare {J X : Type*} [Fintype J] (sqNorm : X → ℝ) :
    List (ℝ × (J → X → X)) → X → ℝ
  | [], v => sqNorm v
  | T :: ts, v => ∑ j, pathSquare sqNorm ts (T.2 j v)

theorem iteratedColumns {J X : Type*} [Fintype J] (sqNorm : X → ℝ)
    (ts : List (ℝ × (J → X → X)))
    (hcol : ∀ T ∈ ts, 0 ≤ T.1 ∧ ∀ v, (∑ j, sqNorm (T.2 j v)) ≤ T.1 * sqNorm v)
    (v : X) :
    pathSquare sqNorm ts v ≤ (ts.map Prod.fst).prod * sqNorm v := by
  induction ts generalizing v with
  | nil => simp [pathSquare]
  | cons T ts ih =>
      have hT := hcol T (by simp)
      have hts : ∀ U ∈ ts,
          0 ≤ U.1 ∧ ∀ v, (∑ j, sqNorm (U.2 j v)) ≤ U.1 * sqNorm v := by
        intro U hU
        exact hcol U (by simp [hU])
      have hprod : 0 ≤ (ts.map Prod.fst).prod := by
        apply List.prod_nonneg
        intro c hc
        obtain ⟨U, hU, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hc
        exact (hts U hU).1
      calc
        pathSquare sqNorm (T :: ts) v =
            ∑ j, pathSquare sqNorm ts (T.2 j v) := rfl
        _ ≤ ∑ j, (ts.map Prod.fst).prod * sqNorm (T.2 j v) :=
          Finset.sum_le_sum (fun j hj => ih hts (T.2 j v))
        _ = (ts.map Prod.fst).prod * ∑ j, sqNorm (T.2 j v) := by
          rw [Finset.mul_sum]
        _ ≤ (ts.map Prod.fst).prod * (T.1 * sqNorm v) :=
          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hT.2 v) hprod
        _ = ((T :: ts).map Prod.fst).prod * sqNorm v := by
          simp only [List.map_cons, List.prod_cons]
          ring

def rightDisplacement (xs : List (ℕ × ℕ)) : ℝ :=
  (xs.map (fun x => (x.1 : ℝ) - (x.2 : ℝ))).sum

def rightBudget (xs : List (ℕ × ℕ)) : ℕ :=
  (xs.map Prod.fst).sum

theorem rightPrefixBudget (xs : List (ℕ × ℕ)) (n : ℕ) :
    rightDisplacement (xs.take n) ≤ (rightBudget xs : ℝ) := by
  induction xs generalizing n with
  | nil => simp [rightDisplacement, rightBudget]
  | cons x xs ih =>
      cases n with
      | zero => simp [rightDisplacement, rightBudget]; positivity
      | succ n =>
          have h := ih n
          simp only [List.take_succ_cons, rightDisplacement, rightBudget,
            List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, Nat.cast_add] at h ⊢
          have hj : (0 : ℝ) ≤ x.2 := by positivity
          linarith

theorem rightEnergyCutoff (xs : List (ℕ × ℕ)) (n : ℕ) (h N : ℝ) (hh : h ≤ N) :
    h + rightDisplacement (xs.take n) ≤ N + (rightBudget xs : ℝ) :=
  add_le_add hh (rightPrefixBudget xs n)

theorem oneModeIndexBound (h h' M : ℝ) (c j : ℕ)
    (hin : h ≤ M) (hout : 0 ≤ h')
    (hshift : h' = h + (c : ℝ) - (j : ℝ)) :
    (j : ℝ) ≤ M + (c : ℝ) := by
  linarith

theorem mixedExponentIdentity (DL DR p q nL nR : ℤ) :
    (2 * DL - p) + (2 * DR - q) + (q - 1) + (p - 1) +
        2 * (nL + nR) =
      2 * (DL + DR + nL + nR - 1) := by
  ring

end

end EnergyBootstrap

statement_fidelity.text:
# Statement fidelity: the finite operator-path core

The declarations in `Main.lean` are in namespace `EnergyBootstrap`.
They do not formalize a vertex operator algebra, an unbounded operator,
Zhu convergence, Mobius covariance, the contraction limits, or strong
locality. The analytic application of this core is a separate argument
in `report.md`; a compiler success does not certify that application.

`graphSchur` quantifies over arbitrary finite left and right types, any
bipartite relation, arbitrary real path weights, and natural row/column
degree bounds r,s. It proves that the square of the sum of products on
the edges is at most r*s times the product of the two sums of squares.
Neither orthogonality of paths nor a bound on Hilbert-space dimension
is a hypothesis. The degree hypotheses are counts, not the inequality
under audit.

`tupleSumCount` quantifies over every natural n,M and every integer target.
Among tuples of length n+1 with entries in {0,...,M}, at most (M+1)^n
have that target sum. Its proof deletes one coordinate and proves the
resulting map injective using the sum equation. Targets outside the
possible range and n=0 are included.

`modeSumSchur` combines those two statements for arbitrary tuple lengths
p+1,q+1, every common index bound M, and every integer target for the
difference of the two tuple sums. The squared count factor is
(M+1)^(p+q), namely (M+1)^(left_length+right_length-2).
The weights are arbitrary real numbers. For the manuscript, specialize
them to the norms of the two operator paths. Constants attached to a
fixed monomial and its binomial coefficients are handled outside Lean.

`iteratedColumns` is an all-length composition result, not a scalar
contraction assumption. It quantifies over any type X, any finite mode
index type J, a real-valued squared-size function, and any finite list
of families of actual maps J -> X -> X with nonnegative column-bound
constants. The hypothesis gives each one-factor sum-of-squared-size
bound at every vector. The conclusion bounds the sum over all composed
paths by the product of those constants times the initial squared size.
Taking X to be the fixed spectral-cutoff Hilbert subspace and squared
size to be the squared norm gives the path-square estimates. Linearity
of the maps is not needed for this stronger elementary statement.

`rightPrefixBudget` and `rightEnergyCutoff` quantify over lists of natural
pairs (c_i,j_i), all prefix lengths, and arbitrary real initial and cutoff
energies h,N with h<=N. The energy increments are c_i-j_i; every prefix
has energy at most N+sum(c_i), irrespective of the j_i. In the application,
c_i=d_i-1 for right modes. Left adjoints have nonpositive increments
and are the zero-budget specialization. Real, rather than integer,
energies include modules with nonintegral lowest conformal weight.

`oneModeIndexBound` uses real input/output energies and natural c,j.
From input<=M, output>=0, and output=input+c-j, it proves j<=M+c.
It supplies the index bound only on a nonzero, nonnegative-energy path.
It does not assume a finite-support property for a full Mobius transform.

`mixedExponentIdentity` is the integer exponent equality after the
path-square estimates, completion counts, and derivative factors are
combined. It is an auxiliary algebraic identity, not a proof of the
operator inequality in isolation.

The source introduces no new axioms and uses no proof placeholders.
Independent review still has to check this translation and its analytic
use in the manuscript audit.
